— personal items —

Let's start with Colombia, where Monday's magnitude seven-point-four quake has become one of the worst disasters the country's seen in years.

The death toll has climbed past two hundred and sixty, with thousands injured and thousands more still unaccounted for.

Rescuers can't even reach the epicentre up in the Chocó region, the government's declared a national emergency, and the shaking was felt as far off as Ecuador and Panama.

Closer to home in the headlines, Russia has released an American military veteran, sending him back to the States after four years locked up on charges his family and US officials call flatly wrongful.

It's a rare bit of thaw in an otherwise frozen relationship, and Washington's quietly chalking it up as a win.

And a hopeful science note to round out the world: researchers have found the adult brain may be far better at healing itself than anyone assumed.

A class of support cells called astrocytes seems to spring into action after an injury, physically rebuilding the wiring that damage tore up.

It's early lab work, but it hints at real repair where we'd written off any hope of it.

On the tech front, the big AI labs stayed quiet overnight — nothing new you'd actually notice out of OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google — so the interesting stuff is bubbling up from open source instead.

The repo everyone's starring this week is an open-source, agentic video-production system: in plain terms, it turns your AI coding assistant into a whole video studio, stacking a dozen pipelines and hundreds of ready-made tools on top of it.

For a founder shipping an app, that's the flavour of thing worth a bookmark — not a flashy chatbot, but plumbing you can actually build on.

And as ever, treat any chatter about Google's top-tier Gemini finally landing as rumour until it's genuinely live.

Clear from sunrise to sunset, around twenty-six first thing, peaking near thirty-three mid-afternoon, and still clinging to the high twenties into the evening.

No rain today, and none on the horizon.

The Meltemi keeps blowing hard from the north — enough to shove you around, nowhere near enough to cool you — and with heat and wind stacked like this, fire risk stays elevated near the hills.

Sunset's around quarter past eight.

— personal items —

Quick health nudge: thirty-three and bone dry will pull the water out of you before you even feel it, so keep a bottle close and sip early — doubly so if you're climbing.

And your learning bite.

Word of the day: flagging — that's sticking a leg out to the side like a kickstand so you don't barn-door off the wall, using balance instead of brute grip to stay on.

And an AI tip worth stealing: when a bug's got you stuck, don't just paste the error in and say "fix it" — hand the model the error plus the surrounding code and ask "what's the root cause?" You'll get an actual diagnosis instead of a lucky guess.

That's Wednesday — hot, windy, and mostly calm on your end.

Grab those games, drink your water, and stay out of the afternoon sun.
